question: A sum of money doubles itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 12 years when the interest is compounded annually. In how many more years will it become eight times of itself?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **x** times in **T** years at compound interest, it becomes **xⁿ** times in **nT** years.

The sum becomes 2 times (x = 2) in 12 years (T = 12).

To become 8 times, we need it to become 2³ times (n = 3).

Total time to become 8 times = 12 × 3 = 36 years.

More years required = Total time − Time already elapsed = 36 − 12 = 24 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A sum doubles itself (becomes 2 times the principal) in 12 years at compound interest.

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T
